title: A Korean chip startup just quadrupled to $2.2bn, betting AI’s next money is outside the data centre.
excerpt: South Korean chip designer DeepX raised the first slice of a Series D at a $2.2bn valuation, four times its last, on AI chips built for robots and devices.
content_html:
A South Korean chip designer few outside the industry have heard of just became a $2.2bn company. DeepX has signed the first tranche of a Series D round that values it at roughly four times its previous mark. And it is not finished raising.

The first slice is about $29m, from existing backers BNW Investment and DS Asset Management, Bloomberg reported. The company is in talks to raise up to $209m more by September. If that closes, DeepX would be worth as much as $2.4bn, a striking jump for a business most consumers will never knowingly use.

The Pangyo-based startup designs chip architecture tuned for AI. Its twist is where those chips are meant to run. Not in the giant data centres that train the biggest models, but on the edge: inside robots, machines and smart electronics. There, power and cost efficiency matter more than raw scale.

The bet against the data centre

Almost all the money in AI silicon has flowed one way, into the data centre and Nvidia’s GPUs. That is where the spending boom lives. DeepX is chasing the other end. As AI moves into physical devices, each one needs a chip that runs models locally. It has to be cheap, and work without pinging the cloud for every decision.

That is a real market only if the devices arrive. DeepX has pointed at robots and smart electronics as its targets. The valuation jump suggests investors believe it can convert the thesis into sales. In April, the company said it had already signed more than 30 mass-production contracts with customers across eight countries.

A crowded, well-funded race

DeepX is not alone in raising against Nvidia from an odd angle. The UK’s Olix is building optical inference chips that skip the components in shortest supply. Xsight raised $300m for the networking chips that wire GPUs together. Even Intel has handed its low-power chip tech to a startup. Edge AI is the newest front.

The caution is the same one that hangs over the whole field. The data-centre build-out still dwarfs everything else, and on-device AI only pays off at scale if robots and smart machines become everyday objects. DeepX is betting they will. For now, investors are willing to quadruple its price to bet alongside it.

content_html_zh:
业内外鲜为人知的一家韩国芯片设计公司刚刚成为一家价值 22 亿美元的公司。 DeepX 已签署 D 轮融资的第一笔款项，其估值约为之前的四倍。 而且它还没有完成。

据彭博社报道，第一笔资金约为 2900 万美元，来自现有支持者 BNW Investment 和 DS Asset Management。 该公司正在商谈在 9 月份之前筹集最多 2.09 亿美元的资金。 如果交易结束，DeepX 的价值将高达 24 亿美元，对于大多数消费者永远不会有意使用的业务来说，这是一个惊人的飞跃。

这家位于 Pangyo 的初创公司设计了专为人工智能而设计的芯片架构。 它的关键在于这些芯片的运行位置。 不是在训练最大模型的巨型数据中心，而是在边缘：机器人、机器和智能电子产品内部。 在那里，电力和成本效率比原始规模更重要。

对数据中心的赌注

几乎所有人工智能芯片的资金都流向了数据中心和 Nvidia 的 GPU。 这就是消费热潮所在。 DeepX 正在追赶另一端。 随着人工智能进入物理设备，每个设备都需要一个在本地运行模型的芯片。 它必须便宜，并且无需为每个决策都对云进行 ping 操作即可工作。

只有设备到达时，这才是真正的市场。 DeepX 将机器人和智能电子产品作为其目标。 估值的跳跃表明投资者相信它可以将论文转化为销售。 4月份，该公司表示已与8个国家的客户签署了30多个量产合同。

一场拥挤、资金充足的比赛

DeepX 并不是唯一一个以奇怪的角度对抗 Nvidia 的公司。 英国的 Olix 正在制造光学推理芯片，跳过供应最短缺的组件。 Xsight 为将 GPU 连接在一起的网络芯片筹集了 3 亿美元。 甚至英特尔也将其低功耗芯片技术交给了一家初创公司。 边缘人工智能是最新的前沿。

整个领域都笼罩着同样的警告。 数据中心的建设仍然让其他一切相形见绌，而设备上的人工智能只有在机器人和智能机器成为日常用品时才能大规模发挥作用。 DeepX 打赌他们会的。 目前，投资者愿意将其价格翻两番来押注。
